title: fix(app-shell): the metadata-admin designer reads and writes visibleWhen only (objectui#12696)
body:
Fixes #12696
Clause-②: no (narrowing)

## Summary

The metadata-admin designer was the last reader and writer of the form view's retired `visibleOn` predicate. objectui#12654 (PR #12692) had already removed it from the console form page, plugin-form and `SchemaRenderer`. After this PR the designer reads and writes `visibleWhen` only:

- **Writer.** `anchors.ts` writes `visibleWhen: "data.viewKind == 'list'"` / `'form'` on the view create schema's `kind` and `formType` pickers.
- **Reader.** `SchemaForm`'s `readVisibility` returns `node?.visibleWhen` and nothing else. The `?? visibleOn` fold is gone from all five call sites: flat create properties, sections, section fields, tab reachability and record-editor sub-fields.
- **Types.** `FormFieldSpec` and `FormSectionSpec` (exported from the `@object-ui/app-shell` entry) drop their `visibleOn` member. `'visibleOn'` stays in `FormSectionSpec`'s `Omit` list, because the spec's input `FormSection` type still carries it and would otherwise re-admit it.
- **Condition widget.** `CONDITION_FIELD_NAMES` drops `'visibleOn'`. A `*When` property still gets the condition builder by name.
- **Prose.** Doc comments that called the predicate `visibleOn` now say `visibleWhen`, in `predicate.ts`, `view-schema.ts`, `page-schema.ts`, `report-schema.ts`, `mergeServerFields.ts`, `PageDefaultInspector.tsx`, `ViewVariantInspector.tsx` and `ReportDefaultInspector.tsx`. The last one is included because objectui#12745 merged before this branch's `origin/main` merge.

## The narrowing (what a host sees)

A host that passes `visibleOn` to `SchemaForm`, on a FormView section, a section field, a record sub-field or a raw JSONSchema property, now sees that node **shown unconditionally**. This matches the runtime form. A typed object literal that sets `visibleOn` on a `FormFieldSpec` or `FormSectionSpec` **no longer compiles** (TS2353). **The fix is one rename: write `visibleWhen`.** The predicate value keeps the same shape. The changeset says the same.

## Measurements behind each step

- **No producer left.** After the anchor change, no non-test file in `packages/` or `apps/` writes `visibleOn` into a FormView or a create schema that SchemaForm reads. The 17 authoring FormViews the bundled spec exports (`viewForm`, `pageForm`, `reportForm`, `objectForm`, `fieldForm`, `actionForm` and others) carry 0 `visibleOn` nodes and 89 `visibleWhen` nodes.
- **Condition widget entry.** No bundled authoring form declares a field named `visibleOn`, while `visible` and `visibleWhen` do appear (the positive control). The spec's JSON schemas still describe a deprecated `visibleOn` property on `FormSection` / `FormField`, but no designer form surfaces that position. So the entry had no named producer and is dropped.
- **Spec version.** The installed `@objectstack/spec` 18.0.0-next.2 still accepts `visibleOn` as a deprecated alias that it folds into `visibleWhen` at parse. objectstack main turns it into a `retiredKey`. Either way, a parsed form reaching the designer carries `visibleWhen`.

## Tests

- `view-create-body.visibility.test.tsx` (new) renders the real registered view create schema and flips `viewKind`. Each picker shows only for its own family.
- The `SchemaForm.visibleWhen.test.tsx` suite named "retired `visibleOn` is not read (objectui#12696)" replaces the old alias suite. A section and a field carrying only `visibleOn` are not hidden. The same predicates under `visibleWhen` are hidden. A raw create property carrying only `visibleOn` is not hidden.
- `view-create-body.test.ts` pins `visibleWhen` on both pickers and the absence of `visibleOn`.
- `form-spec.containers.test.tsx` PIN J refuses `visibleOn` on both types at compile time.
- The alias-spelled fixtures in the flat-visibility, page-visibility and collapsible suites are re-spelled `visibleWhen`; they only used the alias.
- Ablations, each with its restore proven by blob equal to HEAD:
  - Re-spelling the anchor's list gate `visibleOn` makes 2 cases fail.
  - Re-adding the reader's fold makes the 2 retired-key cases fail.
  - Re-adding `visibleOn` on `FormSectionSpec` makes `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` fail with exactly one TS2578, at PIN J.
- Runs at the head this PR opens on:
  - The metadata-admin directory: 517 files, 5805 passed, 1 skipped.
  - Every other test file naming `visibleOn`, `readVisibility`, `FormFieldSpec` or `FormSectionSpec`: 40 files, 889 passed, 1 skipped.
  - `@object-ui/app-shell` and `@object-ui/console` type-check: both green.

## Outside the claimed file surface (forced by the narrowing)

- `apps/console` tests that build these types from object literals:
  - `FormPage.fieldSpec.test.ts` and `FormPage.viewSpec.test.ts`: the `visibleOn` line is dropped from the "was undeclarable here" literal.
  - `FormPage.conditionalRules.test.tsx` and `FormPage.visibleWhen.test.tsx` (#12654's raw retired-key pins): one `@ts-expect-error` line each. Their runtime assertion is unchanged.
- No console source changed.
- `conditionScope.ts` and its test's prose: the restated name list drops `visibleOn`.

## Acceptance notes

- Stale `visibleOn` prose left outside this surface:
  - a comment in `packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordFormPage.tsx` ("per-field `visibleOn` predicates (#2212)");
  - `apps/console/README.md` ("`visible` / `visibleOn` — Expression-based visibility conditions");
  - a `packages/plugin-form/README.md` table row documenting `visibleOn`.
- None of them is filed.
- The spec skew (deprecated alias in 18.0.0-next.2, `retiredKey` on objectstack main) closes with the next spec bump.
